topic: Manipur ethnic violence: houses torched, power worker killed
headline_marked: Electricity worker killed as [[ethnic violence erupts in Manipur]]
headline: Electricity worker killed as ethnic violence erupts in Manipur
summary: Armed attacks on eight villages across Tamenglong, Noney, and Kangpokpi districts left one dead and several homes burned.
details: Armed attackers launched simultaneous raids on at least eight villages across the Tamenglong, Noney, and Kangpokpi districts of Manipur on Wednesday dawn.
The attacks targeted five Naga-dominated and three Kuki-dominated villages, resulting in several houses being set on fire.
Paojangam Chongloi, a 36-year-old electricity worker, was shot and killed while attempting to repair damaged power lines during the unrest.
In the Kuki villages of Lassan, Songpibung, and Ti Kholmun, attackers used heavy weaponry to open fire, leading the village head of Lassan to file a 'zero FIR' at the Kangpokpi police station.
Simultaneously, attacks hit five Naga-dominated villages, including Makui Chamryupiu and Kapningching Mukti, forcing terrified residents to seek shelter in nearby forests.
In Kapningching Mukti, four houses were burned down before armed volunteers from the village mounted a counter-resistance, forcing the attackers to retreat.

Village authorities in Makui Chamryupiu claim that several armed groups, including KNF (P), KNF (N), and KRA, which are under 'Suspension of Operation' agreements with the government, carried out the attacks.
Manipur has a long history of ethnic conflict, which has left thousands homeless and caused significant loss of life and economic devastation across the state.
caption:

Simultaneously, attacks hit five Naga-dominated villages, including Makui Chamryupiu and Kapningching Mukti, forcing terrified residents to seek shelter in nearby forests.

In Kapningching Mukti, four houses were burned down before armed volunteers from the village mounted a counter-resistance, forcing the attackers to retreat.

Village authorities in Makui Chamryupiu claim that several armed groups, including KNF (P), KNF (N), and KRA, which are under 'Suspension of Operation' agreements with the government, carried out the attacks.

topic: Susan Sarandon arrested at anti-Netanyahu protest
headline_marked: Actor [[Susan Sarandon arrested]] at anti-Netanyahu protest in New York
headline: Actor Susan Sarandon arrested at anti-Netanyahu protest in New York
summary: The Oscar winner was among 30 people detained outside UN headquarters as protesters blocked traffic to oppose Israel's military campaign in Gaza.
details: Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon and Emmy winner Hannah Einbinder were among at least 30 people arrested outside United Nations headquarters in New York on Thursday.
The demonstration, organized by Jewish Voice for Peace, took place ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's address to the UN General Assembly.
Around 200 protesters wearing white T-shirts with slogans like "Fund people not bombs" and "Free Palestine" blocked traffic near the UN complex.
Police used loudspeakers to order the crowd to leave, but a core group remained seated in the road, leading officers to remove them using zip ties.
Other detainees included New York City Council member Chi Ossé and Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier.
Inside the UN, Netanyahu faced a hostile reception as dozens of delegates walked out of the General Assembly Hall when he began his speech.
Netanyahu used his address to defend Israel's military actions in Gaza, while Israel continues to reject accusations of genocide.
The UN protest was part of a series of demonstrations across New York city opposing Israel's Gaza campaign and US support for it.
caption:
